items.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: I said, “no, one of these days he’ll remember this and this will be the best lesson I can teach him.”

ctx.x: Well I like to do more than one week so we can get them on some technical things. Go through all the scales and show them how to go from minor scales and playing diminished and half diminished chords and all of that. And to check embouchures and fingerings and all of that. That sometimes I know the teachers tell them this, but when they come from somebody else then they’ll always listen. Oh yeah he said so and so and so and so. So I’d rather do that. And have them play something by ear, a lot of stuff by ear,…

And I say all right now y’all got some harmony. And then they start switching off and doing the sections of the saxophone when we was playing. And I say, “don’t that sound good?” They say, “yeah it sounds good.” And I didn’t go through that with the trumpet section, but the saxophone section, even on “River Niger” they had their harmony going. And some other things. And I try not to do this. Just like that tune that you heard Kent spread out on [scats] “Mac the Knife.” You heard that chorale, that kind of thing?…
